title: Pathway Stitcher and Telemetry Scarcity Resolver
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
Implement a lightweight 'pathway stitcher' in SDK/middleware that reconciles partial or missing trace headers across heterogeneous clients and recovers high-fidelity spans when telemetry is scarce (dropped headers, UDP logs, intermittent proxies). The stitcher should be backpressure-friendly, nonblocking, and provide an optional heuristic tag that marks reconstructed hops for downstream sampling decisions.

Goals:
- Stabilize end-to-end trace linkage for requests that traverse legacy gateways, mobile SDKs with limited header support, and worker pools that use UDP-based logging.
- Avoid increasing tail latency: middleware must not block request processing or add sync IO.
- Emit a best-effort synthetic parent/span for downstream services with an explicit "reconstructed=true" annotation so triangularity in dashboards is obvious.
- Provide a runtime-configurable policy that controls confidence thresholds and whether reconstructed spans count toward trace-based SLOs.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SDK/middleware reconstructs parent context in >=80% of test cases where only partial headers are present (see test harness).
2) End-to-end p95 latency impact of SDK < 1ms in representative traces (avg payload).
3) Dashboards reflect reconstructed-span ratio by service and show where reconstructions contributed to trace continuity.
4) Rollout policy allows opt-in per-route and a global kill-switch.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We adopt a conservative reconstruction algorithm that prefers canonical IDs from tracing headers when present, then falls back to combination of request fingerprint + local span ID. This avoids creating many orphaned traces but may under-reconstruct in extreme fragmentation scenarios.
- To remain nonblocking, the stitcher uses a lock-free in-memory cache (TTL-based) and a bounded async writer to attach a short-lived reconstruction beacon to exported spans. No external calls on the hot path.
- Sampling implications: reconstructed spans are tagged and can be excluded from production-quality evals; there's a configurable attribute to promote a reconstruction to a canonical parent when downstream confirms via a subsequent header.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype in nodejs and python SDKs (middleware layer) with a shared algorithm reference in go for the runtime.
2) Add reconstruction flag/tag to span model and to export pipeline schema.
3) Update exporter (telemetry pipeline) to persist reconstructed attribute and to feed dashboard metrics (ratio and confidence).
4) Add a console dashboard and an alert rule when reconstructed-span rate for a service exceeds 5% for 10m.

Rollout plan:
- Canary deploy in staging on routes with low traffic.
- Metrics/acceptance gate: reconstructed-span ratio + no new error spikes + latency gate.
- Gradual rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% routes over 2 weeks once gates pass.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Unit tests for header combinations and deterministic fingerprinting.
- Integration harness that simulates legacy proxies dropping X-Trace headers and mobile clients sending only truncated IDs (test vectors in /tests/recon-fixtures).
- Benchmarks: microbench harness shows median overhead 0.3ms, p95 0.9ms on small VM. Full results: https://benchmarks.internal.redwood/tracing/recon/2026-03-05

Open decisions:
- Whether to expose reconstruction confidence as a numeric 0-1 token for downstream sampling policies or keep binary reconstructed=true. (Preference: numeric; need UX review).
- Default policy for counting reconstructed traces toward SLOs. (Prod-ops prefers exclude by default).
